title: Hyperelliptic cross-platform acceptance
objective: Provide and execute reproducible exact-digest dynamic/native/standalone/Wasm cross-platform correctness and performance receipts for local-factor, Kummer, and Cantor paths on the named Phase 10 hosts

oracles: Exact canonical digests from Sage.js dynamic/native differential execution

handoff.summary: Pushed complete frozen-source 168f8504 primary and authenticated Wasm receipts for native Windows x64, Linux ARM64, and macOS ARM64. All cross-mode and cross-host exact digests verify. The 08a7383d test-only package overlay passes on all three, Linux ARM64 raw fixed Cantor boundaries are within 4.3%/3.6% of standalone in genera 2/3, resource/cancellation behavior is explicit, and the generated report does not treat unavailable cells as wins.
risks: The lane began at 4ff7d15e while integration advanced substantially. Required local validation records therefore fail on pre-existing lane drift: native export inventory, two strict hyperelliptic lint findings, and packed_integer production-kernel typing. The exact 168f8504 remote builds and focused three-host receipt verifiers pass.

The checked-in standalone benchmark is unavailable on native Windows and macOS because of POSIX static-archive and GNU/ELF linker contracts respectively; native source-transparent and Wasm rows remain covered.
macOS timings are descriptive shared-host evidence because transient GUI/system load was observed. Absolute timing comparisons across architectures are intentionally prohibited.
next_steps: Cherry-pick 3fe04074 onto current integration and rerun architecture, strict, and native validation there, where the unrelated compiler/inventory drift is already resolved.
If a later source commit replaces the 168f8504 freeze, generate new immutable receipts rather than overwriting this series.
Make the standalone linker recipe native to Mach-O and Windows before adding per-host standalone boundary gates on those systems.
